answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded registry that prices each new identity against those already registered. Each agent posts a refundable stake and solves a per-epoch proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many identities its controller holds. Registration writes a crystal record, so no identity can inherit an older reputation, and vouching between siblings earns no weight. A thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes plus rising compute: marginal cost climbs with n while reward stays flat. A lotus needs still water; trust needs a zephyr of false names to cost everything.
